messages:
Olivia Grant: Heads up 3: Redwood legal queue 3: Memento Health sent a vendor packet that mixes DPA, e-discovery, and retention policy asks. They want: whether we will sign their DPA, how long backups are retained (incl. snapshots), if we can support court-ordered e-discovery exports, and whether data residency can be pinned to eu-west-1. PO is conditional on answers.

Samir Patel: Timeline?

Olivia Grant: They asked for answers by Thu COB. If PO delayed >10 days AE wants to be notified.

Avery Lowe: Ill draft the procurement-friendly bullets. Quick Q: do we proactively offer to sign customer DPA or insist on our standard?

Priya Nair: Legal prefers we offer the standard Redwood DPA and sign it for enterprise deals. We can review customer DPA but require legal review; avoid committing to signing arbitrary customer DPA without escalation. Draft line: "Redwood executes our standard DPA; we will review customer-provided DPAs subject to legal approval and potential enterprise amendment."

Samir Patel: For snapshots/backups: Hosted backup retention is 30 days by default, snapshots are kept for 90 days; Dedicated/Private can configure retention longer. We should avoid quoting >90 days for Hosted unless it's an add-on.

Avery Lowe: Noted. What about e-discovery & court orders?

Priya Nair: Legal-approved line: "Redwood responds to lawful process and court orders per our Data Access and Disclosure policy. For Hosted customers we will cooperate and provide export of customer data under legal process; customers may request assistance for collection. For Dedicated/Private customers we provide guidance and can support on-prem data collection. Any production of data in response to third-party legal requests will follow our legal processes and may require notification to the customer unless prohibited by law."

Olivia Grant: Great. Can we confirm eu-west-1 pinning?

Samir Patel: We support region pinning for Hosted customers for certain plans; for Dedicated/Private customers data can be fully kept in-region. For EU residency, ask them to indicate region preference and we'll include region SLA in the enterprise amendment.

Avery Lowe: Drafting final reply: short bullets for DPA, backups, e-discovery, residency + ask them to sign NDA for SOC2/Security artifacts. Also mention export format (JSON/CSV) and that redacted samples available.

Olivia Grant: Please paste before sending and tag @Priya for final sign-off. Also create a task to track PO risk.

OnboardBot: Task created: "Reply to Memento Health vendor packet + track PO risk" assigned to Avery Lowe, due 2026-02-20.

Avery Lowe: Sent reply at 1977771342: pasted bullets (DPA standard + review process; backups retained 30d/90d snapshots for Hosted; Dedicated retention configurable; e-discovery handled via legal process, exports available; EU-region pinning supported for enterprise amendment). Asked them to sign NDA for SOC2/attestations and requested preferred region.

Olivia Grant: Thanks. Flag: if procurement stalls >10 days escalate to AE @Jordan.

Samir Patel: Memento Health acknowledged at 1977771400. Follow-up: they asked whether automated export-and-delete after 30 days is possible (they called it "ephemeral export"). I asked for use-case details and looped in @Priya.

Priya Nair: Automated export-and-delete = enterprise feature; we can offer export workflows and deletion timelines in an amendment. Don't promise automated ephemeral exports in Hosted standard.

Olivia Grant: Perfect. Keeping replies short is helping procurement move. Will update thread if they push evidence requests or DPA redlines.
